summary.headline: Custom macOS compliance settings added to In development
summary.summary: Intune plans custom macOS compliance checks using scripts and JSON rules, with results displayed alongside standard compliance reporting.
summary.adminImpact: Identify custom macOS posture checks that could move into Intune compliance policies when this capability is available.

summary.headline: Corporate identifiers requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The article reformats requirements and explicitly lists Android, iOS/iPadOS, and Windows support plus Policy and Profile Manager or Intune Administrator role requirements.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm admins adding corporate identifiers hold one of the listed roles.

summary.headline: Managed Google Play connection prerequisites clarified
summary.summary: The connection guide now groups country availability, Microsoft Entra account/mailbox, and Intune Administrator or custom organization read/update permissions as requirements.
summary.adminImpact: Verify regional availability, the account mailbox, and required tenant permissions before connecting Managed Google Play.

summary.headline: Android app-management permissions guidance reformatted
summary.summary: The guide preserves the required Managed apps permissions and explains that Application Manager has sufficient permissions and scope tags control administrator visibility.
summary.adminImpact: Validate custom roles include the listed Managed apps permissions before enforcing mobile application management.

summary.headline: User-associated AOSP enrollment requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The AOSP setup guide separates platform, licensing, and tenant requirements and states that specialized-device users need valid licenses.
summary.adminImpact: Assign valid licenses to specialized-device users and review the reorganized AOSP prerequisites before enrollment.

summary.headline: Userless AOSP enrollment requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The userless AOSP guide now separates platform, licensing, and tenant requirements and calls out valid licenses for specialized-device users.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm licensing and tenant prerequisites before enrolling userless AOSP devices.

summary.headline: Corporate-owned work-profile requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The guide reformats its requirements while retaining Android 8.0+, Google Mobile Services connectivity, regional Android Enterprise availability, and device-support checks.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm devices meet Android and GMS prerequisites and Android Enterprise is available before deployment.

summary.headline: Android dedicated-device requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The dedicated-device guide restructures requirements while retaining Android 8.0+, Google Mobile Services connectivity, regional availability, and device support checks.
summary.adminImpact: Continue validating Android version, GMS access, and Android Enterprise support for dedicated devices.

summary.headline: Fully managed Android requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The guide restructures prerequisites while retaining Android 10+, Google Mobile Services connectivity, regional and device support checks, and the existing tenant setup guidance.
summary.adminImpact: Use the organized prerequisites to validate device eligibility and tenant setup before fully managed enrollment.

summary.headline: Personal work-profile requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The guide restructures Android Enterprise availability, tenant connection, and platform support prerequisites into dedicated requirement sections.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm tenant connection and supported device status before enabling personal work-profile enrollment.

summary.headline: iOS/iPadOS ADE prerequisites reorganized
summary.summary: The ADE guide now separately identifies new or wiped Apple Business Manager or School Manager devices and the required Apple portal access, token, and MDM push certificate.
summary.adminImpact: Ensure ADE devices are new or wiped and renew the Apple token and push certificate before policy creation.

summary.headline: macOS ADE prerequisites reorganized
summary.summary: The macOS ADE guide now separates device eligibility from tenant requirements, including Apple portal access, a macOS ADE token, and an Intune MDM push certificate.
summary.adminImpact: Validate new or wiped macOS hardware and current Apple enrollment credentials before creating ADE policies.

summary.headline: Apple TV ADE prerequisites reorganized
summary.summary: The tvOS ADE guide separates eligible new or wiped Apple TV hardware from portal access, active Apple token, and Intune MDM push-certificate requirements.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm Apple TV purchase/reset state and required Apple credentials before setting up ADE.

summary.headline: Apple Configurator enrollment requirements separated
summary.summary: The iOS/iPadOS Configurator guide adds explicit platform and tenant-configuration requirement sections for MDM authority and Apple MDM push certificate.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm MDM authority and a valid Apple push certificate before using Apple Configurator enrollment.

summary.headline: Web-based iOS enrollment requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The guide explicitly states iOS/iPadOS 15+ support, with earlier versions automatically using app-based enrollment, and identifies MDM authority and push-certificate prerequisites.
summary.adminImpact: Target web enrollment to iOS/iPadOS 15+ and plan Company Portal app-based enrollment for version 14.9 and earlier.

summary.headline: Chrome Enterprise connector access requirements clarified
summary.summary: The connector guide now groups Google Admin console and ChromeOS-device-management access with the Intune Service Administrator or equivalent custom-role requirement.
summary.adminImpact: Verify the operator has Google Admin access and the named Intune role or custom permission before connecting Chrome Enterprise.

summary.headline: Enrollment MFA requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The MFA article now explicitly lists Android, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Windows support and states that users need Microsoft Entra ID P1 or later.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm affected users have Entra ID P1 or higher before implementing this enrollment MFA policy.

summary.headline: Device-limit restriction access requirements clarified
summary.summary: The guide lists Android, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Windows support and confirms Intune Service Administrator can create, edit, delete, and reprioritize restrictions; custom and other built-in roles are read-only.
summary.adminImpact: Assign Intune Service Administrator to operators who need to manage device-limit restrictions.

summary.headline: Platform restriction access requirements clarified
summary.summary: The guide lists Android, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Windows support and confirms Intune Administrator can create, edit, delete, and reprioritize platform restrictions while other built-in roles are read-only.
summary.adminImpact: Ensure operators who manage platform restrictions have the Intune Administrator role and apply scope tags as needed.

summary.headline: Device Enrollment Manager role permissions clarified
summary.summary: The guide now structures the Intune Administrator requirement separately and documents Update permission for creating or deleting DEM accounts and Read permission for viewing them.
summary.adminImpact: Give DEM account operators Intune Administrator and verify their required read/update activities.

summary.headline: Enrollment notification prerequisites clarified
summary.summary: The guide now requires Intune Administrator to create enrollment notifications and calls out Intune branding and customization setup under Tenant administration > Customization.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm operator role and configure tenant branding before creating enrollment notifications.

summary.headline: Enrollment time grouping requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The article restructures requirements for Windows Autopilot device preparation, Android Enterprise, and tvOS/visionOS ADE, including the relevant enrollment-time device membership assignment permissions.
summary.adminImpact: Review custom RBAC roles for the needed enrollment-time group-assignment permissions before configuring enrollment time grouping.

summary.headline: Configuration Manager 2603 ARM64 reference corrected
summary.summary: The 2603 What's New article corrects an ARM64 version reference and a troubleshooting URL.
summary.adminImpact: Use the corrected 2603 documentation references when validating ARM64 support or troubleshooting.

summary.headline: Configuration Manager troubleshooting link corrected
summary.summary: The release-notes page updates its troubleshooting link to the Configuration Manager welcome page.
summary.adminImpact: Use the updated troubleshooting landing page when investigating Configuration Manager issues.

summary.headline: Android device-staging requirements reorganized
summary.summary: The device-staging article separates the Android 8+ requirement and supported corporate-owned fully managed and work-profile enrollment methods from its overview.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm Android 8+ and use a supported corporate-owned enrollment profile before enabling staging tokens.
